newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ulster Bank names Wilson as CEO designate.
newsitem.headline: Ulster Bank names Wilson as CEO designate.

text.p: Ulster Bank, the Irish subsidiary of National Westminster Bank Plc, said that it had appointed Martin Wilson as deputy group chief executive with effect from March 31, 1997.
Wilson will assume the role of chief executive of Ulster Bank when the current chief executive, Ronnie Kells, retires in 1998.
Paddy McMahon will succeed Wilson as chief executive of Ulster Bank Markets, the division dealing with treasury, capital markets and corporate investment banking, the bank said in a statement.
Tony McArdle will replace McMahon as head of corporate banking and specialised finance while John McNally has been appointed as deputy chief executive of Ulster Bank's retail division.
He will take over as chief executive from Franklin Adair when he retires.
Richie Boucher succeeds McNally as regional director of the bank's southern region.
Kells said the management structure being put in place would provide an ordered succession at executive level.

"The announcement of the new appointments is timed to demonstrate that a clear strategy has been put in place for filling the key positions in Ulster Bank Group which will become vacant in a relatively short period of time," he said.
